verdict: Nvidia's revenue jumped 56% to $46.7B as its Blackwell AI platform ramped, with Data Center bringing in $41.1B — and it kept $26.4B of that as profit.

segments.name: Data Center
segments.note: AI data-center platforms; a record $41.1B, up 56% YoY and 88% of total revenue. Within it, compute was $33.8B (+50%) and networking $7.3B (+98%) on NVLink fabric for Blackwell systems.

segments.name: Edge Computing
segments.note: Gaming ($4.3B, +49%), professional visualization ($601M, +32%), automotive ($586M, +69%) and OEM and other ($173M, +97%); up 50% YoY in total.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: R&D spending on new chips and platforms; up 39% YoY as Nvidia hires and builds faster.

opex.name: SG&A
opex.note: Sales and admin costs; up 33% YoY, growing far slower than revenue.

otherDetail: Interest income of $592M, plus $2,236M of other income — mostly gains on a publicly-held equity stake Nvidia holds — less $62M of interest expense.
follow100Note: The rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Data Center is nearly the whole company
takeaways.text: Data Center revenue was a record $41.1B — 88 cents of every revenue dollar. Compute brought in $33.8B (+50%) and networking $7.3B (+98%) as Blackwell systems ramped.

takeaways.title: Guidance points higher still
takeaways.text: Nvidia guided third-quarter revenue to $54.0B, plus or minus 2%, with gross margin around 73.3% — and assumed no H20 chip sales to China at all.

takeaways.title: Cash kept pouring in
takeaways.text: Operating cash flow was $15.4B in the quarter. Nvidia returned $10.0B to shareholders ($9.7B of buybacks plus dividends) and the board added $60B to the buyback plan.

oneTimers: A $180M release of previously reserved H20 chip inventory flattered gross profit: without it, non-GAAP gross margin would have been 72.3% rather than 72.7%. There were no H20 sales to China-based customers in the quarter; about $650M of unrestricted H20 chips were sold to a customer outside China.
